_comment: HAND-WRITTEN, never generated. A generated expectation pins whatever the implementation happens to do, including its bugs. Each case states the reasoning that produced its expected tokens. SPEC 5 makes this tokenization normative: changing it requires bumping TOKENIZE_VERSION and re-labelling every previously reported metric.

cases.name: pure_zh_tw
cases.why: one token per ideograph; the embedded latin 'B' is its own run

cases.name: ordinance_id
cases.why: latin and digit runs split on whitespace; both survive as single tokens

cases.name: fullwidth_folds_to_halfwidth
cases.why: NFKC folds fullwidth latin/digits, so this must tokenise identically to ordinance_id's first two tokens

cases.name: punctuation_is_dropped_not_tokenised
cases.why: fullwidth comma folds to ',' and is dropped; the ideographic full stop is dropped as-is; neither becomes a token

cases.name: ext_a_ideograph
cases.why: CJK Extension A is inside IDEOGRAPH_RANGES

cases.name: compat_ideograph_normalises_to_uro
cases.why: U+F900 is a compatibility ideograph; NFKC maps it to its unified form U+8C48, so the token is the URO character

cases.name: kana
cases.why: kana are per-character like ideographs; not expected in a zh-TW corpus, but must not be silently dropped

cases.name: mixed_script_sentence
cases.why: realistic zh-TW with an embedded acronym and a number; casefolded latin, per-char zh
cases.text: 議會以 7 票對 2 票通過 Ordinance 第 123 號。

cases.name: whitespace_collapse
cases.why: normalise collapses runs of whitespace, so spacing cannot change the token stream
cases.text:
我們   搬到
	B  棟

cases.name: empty
cases.why: the tokenizer is total: empty input is an empty token list, never an error
